claim: Connection inquiries are speculative options. The Finnish government is preparing rules that would drop large data centres down the queue, and Fingrid itself notes that connection capacity, not demand, is the constraint. A 24 GW queue cannot convert at anything like face value.

source.name: DCD, Finland to abandon first-come first-served grid connections

claim: Guidance is not delivery. Secondary reporting indicates 30-50% of US projects planned for 2026 are delayed or cancelled, capacity under construction fell 5.7% in 2025, and new announcements halved in Q4 2025. Power, transformers and switchgear, not capital, are the binding constraint.

source.name: Archdesk / tech-insider industry summaries

claim: The rate of increase is collapsing: +93-98% in 1Q26, +58-63% in 2Q26, +13-18% in 3Q26. Long-term agreements now cap increases. Decelerating increments with buyers building inventory for an anticipated 2027 shortage is the pattern that preceded the 2022 memory correction.

claim: Goldman Sachs forecasts copper prices to decline somewhat from record highs during 2026; the September 2026 all-time high failed to hold within days. Speculative positioning from China is cited as a driver, which is cyclical, not demand-based.

source.name: Goldman Sachs Insights; Benchmark Mineral Intelligence

claim: Signed agreements are not energised load. Fingrid states that full implementation would raise Finnish consumption by nearly 40% versus 2025, which is physically implausible on the proposed timelines; the historical conversion rate from signed agreement to energised load is unknown. claim: Record distributor sentiment is a late-cycle marker. In the previous cycle, global semiconductor sales peaked in 2022 (USD 573.5 bn) and turned negative month on month by December 2022 (-4.4%), with memory among the first segments to correct. Analogy, not forecast.

source.name: SIA / WSTS data as summarised by Nomad Semi, State of the Semiconductor Cycle

claim: The EUR 13 bn is scheduled for 2027-2028 and includes energy infrastructure, not only data halls. Relay demand follows substation design and procurement, which lags site announcement by 12-24 months, and the share of spend reaching MV protection equipment is small. [ASSUMPTION: timing lag; verify with ABB how far ahead of energisation relays are ordered.]

claim: Tightness is product-specific. 8-bit MCUs have normalised to 2-10 weeks and DRAM lead times in some trackers are 8-12 weeks and improving. A 52-week figure for one STMicro family does not describe the whole bill of materials.

source.name: Welllink / Lytica state of the components market

claim: Core markets are reopening under conditions: Ireland lifted its de facto moratorium with a framework requiring on-site dispatchable generation and 80% additional Irish renewables. If FLAP-D capacity returns, the regional shift to the Nordics weakens.

claim: The IEA base case is bracketed by alternative cases (Lift-Off, High Efficiency, Headwinds). Efficiency gains in AI hardware and software could materially lower the 2030 figure; the report itself flags this uncertainty.

claim: Fingrid has already restricted new energy-storage connections in Southern Finland until 2029 for lack of connection capacity; data-centre agreements in the south compete for the same capacity and may slip.

source.name: Castren & Snellman: Fingrid extends restrictions on new energy storage facility connections

claim: Delays caused by transformer and switchgear shortages are evidence of demand exceeding electrical supply, not of demand weakness. Switchgear reported sold out through 2028 is a bullish signal for protection equipment, even as project dates slip.

source.name: Same secondary reporting (Archdesk) read in reverse

claim: Fingrid's own study shows the Finnish constraint is grid connectability, not price: 70% of generation sits in the west and north, over 50% of consumption in the south. Cheap power that cannot be connected does not attract load.

source.name: Fingrid news: locating industrial facilities close to generation increases connectability

claim: Land purchases are options. Hyperscalers hold land banks in many countries that remain undeveloped for years; the purchase does not imply a connection agreement or a build date.

claim: Jonathan Koomey and co-authors find that data-centre electricity forecasts are biased toward overestimation: duplicate and speculative interconnection requests inflate expected load, service-demand growth and efficiency gains are both uncertain, and historical utility forecasts have consistently overshot. Projections of explosive growth should be discounted, not taken at face value.
